description: Hi! I’m Takla, a CS and Software Engineering student from Egypt interested in EdTech, space exploration, and smart interactive systems. My skills include React, Electron, Supabase, IoT, Computer Vision, Computer Graphics, and PR leadership. Together, our team is building the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, a gamified space simulator for kids. Our team stands out for its organized communication, creative vision, and focus on shipping a working prototype
summary: Team Smart Galaxy developed Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, an interactive five-player game that turns complex space engineering into a collaborative team mission on Mars.   Traditional space education often falls short because complex books bore young students while existing games are too easy and lack real pressure, preventing students from experiencing the hard decisions required to save a real Mars mission. Our trainer addresses this challenge by placing a five-player crew in emergency scenarios where they communicate via team chat and voice play, receive live guidance from an Earth Agency AI Agent, and vote on shared choices. Crew members must manage limited base power across oxygen, food, and radiation shields—such as stopping the greenhouse to save oxygen even though food drops—teaching the NASA mindset of sacrificing one system to save the crew when no perfect answer exists.   This project is important because it gives students and active youth practical space science labs and real decision-making experience under pressure, while using hidden analytics to help schools, training centers, and space and tech companies discover top young talent and qualify them for certified courses.
details:
Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer (Mars Outpost), developed by Team Smart Galaxy, is an interactive multiplayer space simulation game that teaches students real-world Mars engineering decisions under pressure while helping organizations discover top young talent.

What It Does & How It Works

  • Core Base Simulation: Players manage a Mars outpost across an 8-Sol mission by monitoring five live gauges (Power, Oxygen, Food, Shield, Comfort) and toggling four base systems: Shield, Heater, Grow LEDs, and $\text{O}_2$ Pump.
  • Emergency Crew Voting: During timed crises—dust storms, solar flares, Hab-2 oxygen leaks, and $-90^\circ\text{C}$ freezing nights—a five-player crew votes on shared actions where every decision impacts the entire team.
  • Interactive EVA & AI Guidance: Players move EVA astronauts via an on-screen joystick or keyboard keys (WASD/arrows) and coordinate using team chat, voice play, and a live Ground Station AI Agent.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • For Students & Youth: Replaces boring textbooks and overly easy games with realistic mission pressure, teaching curious students and future astronauts practical survival and decision-making skills through active play.
  • For Schools & Training Centers: Provides schools and academies with practical, interactive space science labs and enables training centers to qualify high-performing youth for certified courses.
  • For Space & Tech Companies: Transforms gameplay into a talent discovery pipeline that identifies smart young thinkers based on how they analyze risks, collaborate, and respond to emergencies.

How the Project Is Creative

  • Real NASA Trade-Off Mindset: Enforces the rule that there is no perfect answer—only smart decisions—requiring crews to sacrifice one system to save another, such as stopping the greenhouse to save oxygen while food drops.
  • Proactive AI & Dynamic Crew Ideas: The Ground Station AI warns the crew 8 seconds before a crisis hits, recommends options to protect the weakest gauge, and evaluates custom player-typed ideas to add feasible solutions to the live vote.
  • Confidential Company Analytics Portal: A PIN-protected Company Portal (company-2026), hidden from players, ranks candidates into Top Talent, Strong, or Developing tiers across Decision Quality, Focus, Foresight, Teamwork, Ideas, and Resilience.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Web Development Stack: Built as a self-contained, zero-dependency web application (project.html) using HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript that runs directly in any modern web browser.
  • Graphics & Physics Engine: Uses CSS glassmorphism (backdrop-filter), conic-gradient ring gauges, embedded Base64 Mars scenery and astronaut sprites, and a requestAnimationFrame loop for real-time astronaut movement.
  • Presentation & Audio Tools: Supported by a structured pitch deck (Final Presentation_2.pptx) and a narrated project demonstration video with audio post-production processed via Auphonic.

Factors Our Team Considered

  • Balancing Fun with Science: Designed to solve why traditional space education fails by combining authentic engineering resource constraints with fast-paced, collaborative gameplay.
  • Bilingual Localization: Engineered with full English and Arabic (عربي) interface support, automatic right-to-left (RTL) layout switching, and bilingual keyword recognition in the Ground Station AI chat.
  • Cross-Device Accessibility: Built with mobile-first responsive styling, touch-enabled pointer events for the virtual joystick alongside desktop keyboard controls, and prefers-reduced-motion accessibility support
